name: Fire hotspots from space
summary: Places where NASA's fire satellites saw heat near each city in the last 24 hours. A hotspot is a heat spot seen from space, not a confirmed fire.
tagline: NASA FIRMS · every 30 min · free key

el.name: Θερμές κηλίδες φωτιάς από το διάστημα
el.summary: Σημεία όπου οι δορυφόροι πυρκαγιών της NASA είδαν θερμότητα κοντά σε κάθε πόλη τις τελευταίες 24 ώρες. Μια θερμή κηλίδα είναι θερμό σημείο από το διάστημα, όχι επιβεβαιωμένη φωτιά.

publisher.name: NASA FIRMS (LANCE, operated by NASA ESDIS)

licence.attribution: Fire data: NASA FIRMS, provided by LANCE FIRMS operated by NASA ESDIS with funding provided by NASA Headquarters

restrictions: Needs a free NASA FIRMS MAP_KEY; the limit is 5,000 requests per 10 minutes per key (we make 4 every 30 minutes)
NASA's disclaimer says the data are not advised for tactical decisions or for conditions at a local scale
Never say or suggest that NASA endorses this site

coverage.area: Cyprus and nearby sea (box 31.3 to 34.9 E, 33.7 to 36.1 N)

update.note: Satellites pass a few times a day; their data reach FIRMS up to about 3 hours after a pass.

variables.note: Places (repeat sightings merged) within 25 km of the city centre, last 24 hours.
Places (repeat sightings merged) within 50 km of the city centre, last 24 hours.
Distance to the closest hotspot within 100 km. No value when there is none.

quality.uncertainty: A hotspot is a heat spot seen at one moment in a pixel 375 m to 1 km wide: a place, not a confirmed fire. Positions are good to about 1 km. None seen does not mean no fire.
known_issues: A hotspot is a heat anomaly, not a confirmed fire: gas flares, industry (for example power and cement works), sun glint and farm burning also show up
Each satellite passes only a few times a day, so a short fire between passes is never seen; the passes are hours apart
Cloud, thick smoke or tree cover can hide a fire, and very small fires are missed
Low-confidence detections are dropped for every satellite, so a real but faint fire can be missing (the confidence labels are NASA's)
Counts are places, not detections: one place seen again within 1 km, by any satellite at any time in the 24 hours, counts once
NASA's page says Suomi NPP no longer delivers new data; NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS carry the feed
NASA says these data are not advised for tactical decisions or for conditions at a local scale: call 112 if you see smoke or fire

upstream.name: NASA FIRMS active fire detections (VIIRS 375 m on Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21; MODIS 1 km on Terra and Aqua)

use_for: Saying how many places near a city a satellite saw heat in the last 24 hours, and how far the closest is
not_for: Saying that there is, or is not, a fire
Saying a place is safe because no hotspot was seen
Smoke or air quality: this layer shows heat only

notes: Read from the FIRMS pages, never run against the live service from our build sandbox. The key is optional: with no FIRMS_MAP_KEY the layer stays Planned. Licence: NASA says its data are open with no restrictions (CC0 for NASA-led missions); NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 are NOAA missions, so a teacher may want to confirm.

x_rules.window: 24 hours that end when the lists were fetched
x_rules.confidence: low is dropped for every sensor: VIIRS letter l; MODIS under 30 percent. Nominal and high are kept
x_rules.same_row: same sensor, place and time counts once
x_rules.hotspot: any kept detections within 1 km of a seed (best confidence, then newest) are one hotspot, whatever the sensor or the time; not chained
